name: Lock-Free Empty Drain

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Lock-Free Empty Drain Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

Every source edit drains `preview`, `changes` and `count_changed`, every `OrderedEmitter::update` drains even when it computed nothing, and two of a source's three queues are usually empty; each empty drain still locks the queue mutex. Mirroring the queue length into an atomic (updated under the lock on push/pop, in the queue's shared allocation) lets `drain` return without locking when nothing is pending. A push racing with that check drains its own item, and items left by a panicking subscriber keep the count non-zero, so the next drain still delivers them.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** atomic pending count checked before `drain` locks.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/primitives/delivery.rs`.
**Forbidden in this experiment:** callers skipping drains, push changes beyond the counter, subscriber-count logic.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

`primitives::tests` (ordered and panic-safe delivery), full lib + integration tests; clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` (cache/list updates, signal set) and `operator_updates` vs base, rerun borderline. Pass: cache-hot/update-no-subscribers or update-connect >=8% faster; no regression >10% on rerun.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

One to two fewer mutex round trips per source edit.
